purpose: Cysteamine is used to treat a rare genetic condition called cystinosis, where a substance called cystine builds up and damages organs like the kidneys and eyes. It helps protect your organs by lowering the amount of cystine in your body. Eye drop forms are used specifically to treat cystine crystals that form in the eyes.
how_it_works: In cystinosis, cystine gets trapped inside your cells and builds up to harmful levels. Cysteamine works by entering your cells and breaking apart the cystine, turning it into a form that can escape the cell and be removed from your body. Think of it like a key that unlocks and releases the trapped substance so your body can get rid of it.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, loss of appetite, bad breath or body odor, tiredness, and fever are the most common side effects. The eye drops may cause temporary eye stinging, redness, or blurred vision.
warnings: Cysteamine can cause serious skin and bone problems with long-term use, such as skin lesions or fragile bones, so your doctor will monitor you regularly. It can also affect your nervous system, causing seizures or changes in behavior. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, because stopping can cause cystine levels to rise quickly and harm your organs. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some can interact with cysteamine.
typical_dosing: For capsules or tablets, dosing is based on your body weight and is usually taken every 6 hours (Cystagon) or every 12 hours (Procysbi, the long-acting form). Eye drops are typically used several times a day in each eye. Your doctor will find the right dose for you based on blood tests that measure cystine levels in your white blood cells.
